page: Microsoft Azure D64ds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by a 32-core, 64-thread Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Hardware features include 260 MB of L3 cache along with support for vector and matrix extensions such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX. The instance is configured with 256 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU.

Storage configuration includes 3,780 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD capacity, providing low-latency ephemeral disk space alongside support for Azure Premium Storage. The server type contains no discrete GPU hardware accelerators, relying entirely on the Intel Xeon CPU for general compute and CPU-based instruction sets.

Performance testing reflects strong compute and data processing capabilities. Multi-core testing shows a PassMark CPU score of 67,787.17 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 17,892.0. In database and I/O workloads, the instance achieved 24,055.67 on PassMark database operations, 75.07 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations, and 94.85 GB/sec in static web serving throughput, placing it in the top decile. Cached memory read throughput reached 4,212.73 GB/sec, though uncached memory access settled at 149.32 GB/sec read and 69.85 GB/sec write, accompanied by a lower comparative PassMark memory score.

Given its combination of high vCPU density, vector extensions, and integrated NVMe capacity, the D64ds_v6 demonstrates balanced resource efficiency for parallel execution. Primary workload fits include enterprise web serving, relational databases, distributed in-memory caching, software compilation, and CPU-driven machine learning inference.
description: Microsoft Azure D64ds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 64 vCPUs and 32 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz. Powered by Microsoft Hyper-V on an x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 256 GB of RAM, adhering to a 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio, and includes advanced vector extensions such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX. While it lacks a GPU accelerator, it incorporates 3,780 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage. Benchmark results show high multi-core compute capability, with strong PassMark CPU scores of 67,787.17, database operations of 24,055.67, and 75.07 million Redis operations per second. Static web serving throughput reaches top-tier levels at 94.85 GB/sec, although large-block uncached memory operations show average throughput. This configuration offers balanced resource density and high local storage throughput, making it suitable for enterprise web serving, relational databases, distributed caching, software builds, and CPU inference.
